```{r setup}
#| include: false
# Made by scripts/95_region_page.R (one page per candidate set, parameter set_id), from the
# figures and tables it writes to figs/. CONUS ("full") files are used when present, else dev.
id <- params$set_id
k <- as.integer(sub(".*_k", "", id))
label <- params$label
figs <- if (file.exists("figs/manifest.csv")) utils::read.csv("figs/manifest.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) else
  data.frame(figure = character(), profile = character())
pick_file <- function(pattern) {                 # pattern with one %s for the profile
  for (pr in c("full", "dev")) { f <- sprintf(pattern, pr); if (file.exists(f)) return(f) }
  NULL
}
read_fig_csv <- function(what) {
  f <- pick_file(paste0("figs/regionpage_", id, "_", what, "_%s.csv"))
  if (is.null(f)) NULL else utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
}
show_fig <- function(name, caption, alt = caption) {
  m <- figs[figs$figure == name, , drop = FALSE]
  pick <- intersect(c("full", "dev"), m$profile)
  pick <- pick[file.exists(sprintf("figs/%s_%s.png", name, pick))]
  if (!length(pick)) {
    cat(sprintf('\n::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}\n## Figure pending\n%s\n:::\n\n', caption))
    return(invisible())
  }
  r <- m[m$profile == pick[1], ][1, ]
  note <- sprintf("[%s · %s · figure made %s]{.fig-meta}", r$extent, r$years, r$made)
  cat(sprintf('\n![%s %s](figs/%s_%s.png){#fig-%s fig-alt="%s" .column-page-right}\n\n',
              caption, note, name, pick[1], gsub("_", "-", name), alt))
}
kable <- function(x, caption, align = NULL) {
  cat(knitr::kable(x, row.names = FALSE, caption = caption, align = align), sep = "\n"); cat("\n\n")
}
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x)

# crosswalks with the comparison sets
xw_files <- list.files("figs", sprintf("^regionpage_%s_xw_.*_(full|dev)\\.csv$", id), full.names = TRUE)
xw_files <- xw_files[order(!grepl("_full\\.csv$", xw_files))]
xw <- list()
for (f in xw_files) {
  d <- utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (!nrow(d) || d$compare_set[1] %in% names(xw)) next
  xw[[d$compare_set[1]]] <- d
}
set_lab <- function(sid) {
  p <- sub("_k[0-9]+$", "", sid); kk <- as.integer(sub(".*_k", "", sid))
  lab <- c(A1_groups = "Climate A1", A2_groups = "Climate A2", A2_herbw = "Climate A2 herb-weighted",
           A3_groups = "Climate A3", B_raw = "Satellite (level + shape)", B_shape = "Satellite (timing)",
           geo = "Location only")
  sprintf("%s, %d regions", if (p %in% names(lab)) lab[[p]] else p, kk)
}
working <- "A2_groups_k13"
```

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## A candidate set, not the working regions
This page shows **`r label`** so it can be compared with the working regions.
The working regions are still **climate A2 at 13 regions, nested in 7** (decided October 9).
The phenology rules, the typical-date maps and the companion studies use those numbers.
Everything here comes from the existing analysis: k-means was fitted to the same climate
features for every number of regions from 4 to 30, and the tests were run for 4 to 20.
Results are **preliminary**.
The main project page has the methods and the full comparison:
[Fuel phenology regions for herbaceous fuels](index.html).
:::

## How these regions were made

The regions group 4 km grid cells across the contiguous US by their climate. The climate
comes from daily PRISM data (2001–2025), summarized for each year and then across years:

- seasonal temperature, precipitation, aridity and freeze dates (Block 1)
- the timing and variability of rain events, dry spells and the warm-season rain onset
  (Block 2, used by the A2 sets)

Cells are clustered with k-means, here into `r k` groups. The satellite seasonal curves
(MODIS NDVI and NDII7) and the ground observations play no part in drawing the regions.
They are used only to describe and test them.

Region numbers are matched to the project-page maps, so a number covers roughly the same
area wherever it appears. Numbers run roughly south to north, but they do not match the
working regions' numbers. The tables below give the crosswalk.

## Map and what each region contains

```{r map}
#| results: asis
show_fig(paste0("prof_map_", id), paste0(label, "."), sprintf("Map of the contiguous US with %d numbered regions.", k))
```

```{r composition}
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(xw[[working]])) {
  d <- xw[[working]]
  rows <- lapply(sort(unique(d$region)), function(j) {
    e <- d[d$region == j & d$share_of_region >= 0.05, ]
    e <- e[order(-e$share_of_region), ]
    part <- ifelse(e$share_of_compare < 0.8, sprintf(", %s of it", pct(e$share_of_compare)), "")
    data.frame(Region = j,
               `Working regions it contains (share of this region)` =
                 paste(sprintf("%d %s (%s%s)", e$compare_region, e$compare_name, pct(e$share_of_region), part),
                       collapse = "; "),
               check.names = FALSE)
  })
  kable(do.call(rbind, rows),
        sprintf("What each of the %d regions contains, in terms of the 13 working regions (parts holding at least 5 %% of a region's cells; \"x %% of it\" = only part of that working region falls here)", k))
}
for (sid in setdiff(names(xw), working)) {
  d <- xw[[sid]]
  rows <- lapply(sort(unique(d$region)), function(j) {
    e <- d[d$region == j & d$share_of_region >= 0.05, ]; e <- e[order(-e$share_of_region), ]
    data.frame(Region = j, Contains = paste(sprintf("%d (%s)", e$compare_region, pct(e$share_of_region)), collapse = ", "))
  })
  out <- do.call(rbind, rows); names(out)[2] <- sprintf("%s: regions it contains (share of this region)", set_lab(sid))
  kable(out, sprintf("The same comparison with %s (region numbers as on the project page)", set_lab(sid)))
}
```

```{r splits}
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(xw[[working]])) {
  d <- xw[[working]]
  sp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, d$compare_region), function(e) {
    e <- e[e$share_of_compare >= 0.05, ]; e <- e[order(-e$share_of_compare), ]
    data.frame(`Working region` = sprintf("%d %s", e$compare_region[1], e$compare_name[1]),
               `Goes to (share of the working region)` = paste(sprintf("%d (%s)", e$region, pct(e$share_of_compare)), collapse = ", "),
               split = e$share_of_compare[1] < 0.8, check.names = FALSE)
  }))
  n_split <- sum(sp$split)
  cat(sprintf("Of the %d working regions, **%d fall mostly (80 %% of their cells or more) in one of the %d regions** and **%d are split** between two or more.\n\n",
              nrow(sp), nrow(sp) - n_split, k, n_split))
  sp$split <- NULL
  kable(sp, sprintf("Where each working region goes in the %d regions", k))
}
```

## Climate and satellite season by region

The table gives region medians across cells. Season dates come from the satellite record
(MODIS 2001–2025). Where a region has at least 200 strict herbaceous cells, the dates use
those cells; otherwise they use all of the region's cells, which mostly describe forest,
cropland or mixed cover.

```{r profile-table}
#| results: asis
f <- pick_file(paste0("figs/prof_table_", id, "_%s.csv"))
if (!is.null(f)) {
  t <- utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  kable(t, sprintf("%s: median climate and satellite season by region", label), c("r", rep("r", ncol(t) - 2), "l"))
} else cat("\n*Table pending (run scripts/95_region_page.R).*\n\n")
```

```{r heat}
#| results: asis
show_fig(paste0("prof_heat_", id),
         "Region medians of the climate features and satellite season metrics (all cells), coloured by how far each region is above (orange) or below (blue) the average across regions.",
         "Heatmap of climate features and season metrics by region, with median values.")
```

## Satellite seasonal curves

```{r curves}
#| results: asis
show_fig(paste0("prof_curves_", id),
         "Median NDVI (greenness) and NDII7 (canopy water, a curing signal) seasonal curves per region, with the middle half of the cells shaded. Herbaceous cells where a region has enough of them; the dotted line is NDVI for all of the region's cells.",
         sprintf("%d small charts of seasonal NDVI and NDII7 curves, one per region.", k))
```

A region with a wide shaded band holds cells whose seasons differ. That is the cost of
using fewer regions. Compare the bands with the 13-region curves on the project page.

## Ground observations by region

```{r obs}
#| results: asis
show_fig(paste0("prof_obs_", id),
         "Ground observation dates by region: each dot is one site (its median date across years); the bar is the region median and the number is the count of sites.",
         "Dot plots of observed phenology dates by region.")
ob <- read_fig_csv("obs")
if (!is.null(ob) && nrow(ob)) {
  olab <- c(grass_greenup = "NPN grasses: green-up", grass_curing = "NPN grasses: curing",
            grass_cured = "NPN grasses: cured", lfmc_herb_peak = "LFM herbaceous: peak",
            lfmc_woody_peak = "LFM woody: peak", inat_flower = "iNaturalist flowering")
  ob <- ob[ob$set %in% names(olab), ]
  st <- intersect(names(olab), unique(ob$set))
  w <- data.frame(`Data set` = unname(olab[st]), check.names = FALSE)
  for (j in seq_len(k)) w[[paste("Region", j)]] <- vapply(st, function(s) {
    n <- ob$n_sites[ob$set == s & ob$region == j]; if (length(n)) as.integer(n[1]) else 0L }, 0L)
  kable(w, "Number of ground sites per region")
}
```

## How this number of regions scores

These are the tests used to choose the working regions, read at `r k` regions and set next
to the working sets. Two things to keep in mind:

- **More regions always explain more.** A fair comparison is with the location-only
  baseline at the same number of regions: k-means on map position alone, with no climate.
- **The ground scores use few sites,** so differences of a few hundredths are within noise.

```{r scores}
#| results: asis
sc <- read_fig_csv("scores")
if (!is.null(sc) && nrow(sc)) {
  sc$col <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(sc)), function(i) set_lab(sprintf("%s_k%02d", sc$partition[i], sc$k[i])), "")
  # columns: this k first, then the comparison k's; at each k the climate set, then location only
  ks_ord <- unique(c(k, sort(unique(sc$k))))
  ord <- unlist(lapply(ks_ord, function(kk) {
    e <- unique(sc[sc$k == kk, c("partition", "col")])
    e$col[order(e$partition == "geo", e$col)]
  }))
  tl <- c(satellite = "Satellite season (share of variance explained by region)",
          ground = "Ground dates (adjusted R², site dates ~ region)",
          synchrony = "Year-to-year synchrony, herbaceous cells (share of yearly anomalies shared within a region)",
          stability = "Stability of the regions")
  for (tt in intersect(names(tl), unique(sc$test))) {
    d <- sc[sc$test == tt, ]
    ms <- unique(d$measure)
    out <- data.frame(Measure = ms, check.names = FALSE)
    for (cc in ord) out[[cc]] <- vapply(ms, function(m) {
      v <- d$value[d$measure == m & d$col == cc]
      if (!length(v) || is.na(v[1])) "" else if (grepl("Smallest", m)) format(round(v[1]), big.mark = ",") else sprintf("%.2f", v[1])
    }, "")
    out <- out[, c(TRUE, colSums(out[, -1, drop = FALSE] != "") > 0), drop = FALSE]
    kable(out, tl[[tt]], c("l", rep("r", ncol(out) - 1)))
  }
} else cat("\n*Scores pending (run scripts/95_region_page.R).*\n\n")
```

## Notes

- The regions are drawn from climate alone. Fuels, vegetation type and soils are not
  inputs. A comparison with LANDFIRE fuel models is planned separately.
- k-means regions need not be contiguous: a region can include outlying patches with a
  similar climate elsewhere, mostly in mountains.
- Satellite dates are for 4 km cells, which often mix cover types. Ground sites are
  points, and several regions have few of them.
- This page is generated, so every set of regions gets the same layout:
  `Rscript scripts/95_region_page.R full <partition> <k>`.
